events.description: Tom Joscelyn testified before the Senate Armed Services Committee and the Senate Banking Committee on Afghanistan, Taliban leverage and aid.
ISKP suicide bombing of a Hazara Shia mosque in Kunduz by a Uyghur bomber, as part of ISKP campaign against Shiites and wedge against Taliban/al-Qaeda/TIP.
US-Taliban Doha withdrawal deal signed under the Trump administration.
President Biden decided to withdraw US forces from Afghanistan.
Noor Wali Mehsud renewed TTP allegiance to Hibatullah Akhundzada days after the Taliban consolidated victory over the Afghan government.
Taliban jailbreaks freed many Pakistani Taliban prisoners held by the Afghan government, including Fakir Mohammed.
Hakimullah Mehsud killed; Fazlullah selected TTP emir, reportedly with Afghan Taliban/Haqqani/al-Qaeda role.
Bin Laden files recovered in Abbottabad show al-Qaeda negotiating with Pakistani state for ceasefires, working with Sirajuddin Haqqani.
TTP reconfiguration: nine groups rejoined under Noor Wali Mehsud, including two al-Qaeda groups.
Ibrahim al-Qosi (AQAP) video gloating over US withdrawal and threatening America.
The Doha deal between the US and the Taliban. The hosts say some US officials lied on the Taliban's behalf about its al-Qaeda ties. The date is not given in this chunk.
Senate hearings at which Tom Joscelyn testified and generals testified. The hosts say senators recognized the Taliban-al-Qaeda relationship is unbroken.

key_claims: US aid to Pakistan (more than $30bn since 2001) gave Washington zero leverage over Pakistan or the Taliban, so aid to the Taliban will not either.
The Afghan Taliban is a cohesive, centrally organized group, while the TTP is more a confederation of groups.
Noor Wali Mehsud has reunited about nine groups, including two al-Qaeda groups, into the TTP, and TTP attacks have increased in the past year.
Al-Qaeda and the Haqqanis used the TTP as a wedge and cutout to pressure Pakistan, with Sirajuddin Haqqani as a negotiating contact per the Abbottabad files.
The ISKP Kunduz bombing by a Uyghur attacker exploits two wedge issues: anti-Shia violence and Taliban ties to China/Uyghurs and TIP.
ISKP is not an existential threat to the Taliban, but it challenges Taliban legitimacy; the Taliban will likely absorb some ISKP members and crack down on others.
The Taliban continues to lie about ties to al-Qaeda, and there is no evidence the Taliban has betrayed al-Qaeda.
The wheel of jihad: Pakistan backs the Taliban and Haqqanis, who are tied to al-Qaeda and the TTP, which in turn attacks Pakistan.
The Afghan Taliban are themselves a jihadist group and have long been allied with other jihadist groups.
The Taliban lie to this day about al-Qaeda's presence in Afghanistan.
The Taliban-al-Qaeda relationship is unbroken, and there is no evidence the Taliban betrayed al-Qaeda.
Groups such as the TTP and TIP want their share of power in Pakistan and China respectively, which the Taliban must manage.
Some US officials lied on the Taliban's behalf over the Doha deal, but few senators at the hearings did.
The hosts argue for accountability from US generals and officials over the failed Afghanistan policy.
